newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SGS says wins tax appeal on stock buybacks.
newsitem.headline: SGS says wins tax appeal on stock buybacks.

text.p: Swiss group Societe Generale de Surveillance Holding SA (SGS), the world leader in inspections and testing, said a Swiss tax panel had confirmed SGS's position in a dispute over the tax treatment of share buybacks.

The Swiss Federal Appeals Commission for Tax Matters on May 7 upheld SGS's stance that issuing put options to shareholders in such a case does not represent a taxable distribution subject to the 35 percent withholding tax, SGS said in a statement.
The withholding tax applies only to the share repurchase itself and not to the put options as well, an SGS spokesman explained. Federal tax authorities can appeal within 30 days.

The SGS spokesman said the company, which launched share buyback schemes in 1993 and 1996, remained "very interested" in such programmes because it held substantial liquidity that was not fully required for acquisitions or expansion.
But he added market conditions would determine whether SGS would buy back more shares. "It is not carved in stone that we would actually do something," he said.
